label: Q-01
title: toStableAmount is a decimals-only rescale and is not a phUSD preview; the local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals()
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.
justification: QA. toStableAmount is a decimals-only input rescale, not a phUSD preview, and its name invites the opposite reading; the local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals(). No exploit path. Worth reporting because the absence of a real preview is what leaves callers with no way to form the expectation F-01 says they cannot assert on.
recommendation: (a) Add previewAnnihilate(address stable, uint256 amount) returns (uint256 stableAmount, uint256 phUSDOut) composing minter.calculateMintAmount, and document toStableAmount as the input-side rescale only. (b) Rename the local to `stableDecimals`.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

items.(a) missing preview: toStableAmount is the only public preview on the annihilation path and ignores exchangeRate entirely, while the phUSD actually delivered is amount + floor(amount*exchangeRate/1e18). At any rate != 1e18 an integrator deriving an expected payout from this function is wrong on the stable leg. The asymmetry is by design and internally coherent (stable leg priced at rate, antimatter leg always at 1) - the QA item is the ABSENCE of a matching phUSD-side preview.
items.(b) shadowing: The local `decimals` at :250 shadows the inherited ERC20.decimals()/IERC20Metadata.decimals().

additionalContext.note: The economic consequence of an unbounded, un-timelocked exchangeRate is DEDUP-005, deliberately not re-adjudicated here.

mergeAction: SA-006 (slither shadowing-local, confidence high) consolidated into CODE-007(b) - the same variable at the same line. CODE-007 is the stronger framing because it explains why shadowing matters HERE (inside toStableAmount `decimals` means the STABLECOIN's decimals, on the single most safety-critical line in the contract - see DEDUP-003).
